title: First 30 days
summary: Pass in hand, bank open, longer housing underway. This is when Singapore starts to feel operational.

items.title: Collect your Employment Pass / Dependant Pass card
items.detail: Attend the MOM appointment with the documents HR listed. Photograph both sides of the card once issued.

items.title: Open a local bank account
items.detail: DBS, OCBC, UOB, or Standard Chartered are common. Bring passport, pass, IPA, and proof of address. Ask HR if payroll has a preferred bank.

items.title: Confirm CPF / foreign-worker levy status with HR
items.detail: Most EP holders do not contribute to CPF. Know what is deducted and what is not so salary slips make sense.

items.title: Start the longer-term housing search
items.detail: Decide condo vs HDB eligibility, budget, and agent engagement. Walk neighbourhoods at night before signing.

items.title: Set a proper telco plan
items.detail: Move off tourist SIMs onto a postpaid or longer prepaid plan once your address is stable enough for billing.

items.title: Enquire at shortlisted schools (if with kids)
items.detail: International school waitlists move slowly. Tour, ask about mid-year entry, and get fee schedules in writing.

items.title: Register with a GP and review insurance
items.detail: Confirm inpatient vs outpatient cover, panel clinics, and maternity/mental-health riders if relevant.

items.title: Decide on driving licence conversion
items.detail: Foreign licence conversion windows are time-bound. If you will drive, start the conversion process before the grace period closes.

items.title: Book one social or club intro
items.detail: A chamber mixer, nationality association coffee, or hash run. Belonging is a 30-day problem, not a year-three problem.
